steps.say: Tetralogy of Fallot is one malalignment with four consequences. Anterocephalad deviation of the infundibular septum crowds the right ventricular outflow while opening a large subaortic ventricular septal defect beneath an overriding aorta. The right ventricle then keeps hypertrophying against the obstruction it cannot bypass.
steps.tx: **Anterocephalad deviation of the infundibular septum** produces the classic **tetralogy four components** of **Tetralogy of Fallot**: large **subaortic VSD**, **overriding aorta**, **right ventricular outflow obstruction**, and **right ventricular hypertrophy**. The malaligned septum simultaneously uncouples the aorta and narrows the pulmonary path. Hypertrophy follows as the pressure loaded ventricle thickens against fixed resistance.

steps.say: Cyanosis in Fallot is not fixed; it tracks the outflow obstruction. The tighter the subpulmonic and valvular narrowing, the larger the right to left shunt across the defect and the bluer the child. Spells, feeding, and crying all tighten the infundibulum further and deepen the blue within minutes.
steps.tx: The **determinant of cyanosis** is the severity of **subpulmonic and valvular right ventricular outflow obstruction**, which sets the magnitude of the **right to left shunt** and the degree of **cyanosis**. Mild obstruction keeps flow left to right with a pink child, while severe obstruction reverses the shunt and blues the lips. Dynamic infundibular spasm explains why a previously pink infant can turn deeply blue during crying or feeding.

steps.say: The chest film in Fallot has a famous silhouette. Right ventricular hypertrophy lifts the apex upward while an empty pulmonary bay hollows the left border, giving the boot shaped heart called coeur en sabot. Lung fields look dark because pulmonary blood flow is reduced.
steps.tx: The **boot shaped heart (coeur en sabot)** shows an **upturned apex** from **right ventricular hypertrophy** with a concave **pulmonary bay**. Diminished vascular markings reflect reduced **pulmonary blood flow**. About **25 percent** of patients add a **right sided aortic arch**, which the film confirms and the surgeon must know before opening the chest.

vis.alt: A composite image showing X-rays of boot-shaped heart (TOF) and egg-on-string (TGA), with an illustration of a child squatting during a cyanotic spell.
vis.caption: Cyanotic congenital heart disease: classic radiological signs and clinical presentation.

steps.say: Fallot travels with recognisable company, including arch and genetic patterns. A right aortic arch appears in roughly a quarter of cases, an important detail for surgical planning. Microdeletion of chromosome 22q11.2 affects 15 percent of isolated Fallot and climbs to 40 to 50 percent when pulmonary atresia or absent pulmonary valve joins it.
steps.tx: A **right aortic arch** is present in approximately **25 percent** of Fallot patients and alters cannulation and arch repair strategy. **Chromosome 22q11 deletion (DiGeorge/velocardiofacial microdeletion)** occurs in **15 percent** of isolated TOF and in **40-50%** of TOF with **pulmonary atresia** or **absent pulmonary valve**. Palatal, calcium, immune, and learning issues in the same child should trigger deletion testing.

steps.say: Watch a Fallot child at play and you will see self treatment. During exertion these children squat, which kinks the femoral arteries and raises systemic vascular resistance. Higher body resistance shrinks the right to left shunt and pushes more blood through the lungs, so the blue fades.
steps.tx: **Squatting** during exertion increases **systemic vascular resistance**, thereby decreasing **right to left shunting** and promoting **pulmonary blood flow**. Toddlers discover the posture themselves and adopt it before they can explain why. Knee chest positioning during a hypercyanotic spell applies the same physiology while drugs and oxygen are prepared.

nodes.label: Squatting kinks arteries and raises body resistance
Right to left shunt shrinks across the defect
Pulmonary flow rises and cyanosis fades

steps.say: The Fallot murmur keeps misleading beginners who blame the hole. The sound comes solely from right ventricular outflow stenosis as a systolic ejection murmur at the mid to upper left sternal border. The ventricular septal defect itself is large and non restrictive, so it makes no sound at all.
steps.tx: On **auscultation in TOF**, the murmur is caused solely by **RVOT stenosis**: a **systolic ejection murmur** at the **mid to upper left sternal border**. The **VSD is large and non restrictive (silent)** because equal pressures sit on both sides of it. Murmur intensity tracks forward pulmonary flow, so a quieter murmur with deeper cyanosis warns of a tightening outflow, not improvement.

rows: Systolic ejection murmur, upper left border

steps.say: Listen for the second sound and one half is missing. The pulmonary component is markedly delayed and inaudible because almost no blood crosses the valve, leaving a single second heart sound. A loud aortic component stands alone where two sounds should be.
steps.tx: The **second heart sound is typically single** because the **pulmonary component (P2)** is markedly **delayed and inaudible**. Minimal pulmonary flow leaves nothing to slam the valve shut. A single loud S2 with a systolic ejection murmur and cyanosis points strongly toward Fallot before the echo probe touches the chest.

nodes.label: Severe outflow obstruction starves pulmonary flow
Pulmonary valve closure makes no audible sound
Aortic closure stands alone as a single S2

steps.say: Put the pieces together and Fallot announces itself. Boot shaped silhouette, single second sound, ejection murmur, and squatting all trace back to one deviated septum. Complete repair closes the defect, opens the outflow, and lets the hypertrophied ventricle remodel over the years that follow.
steps.tx: Complete repair closes the **VSD**, relieves the **outflow obstruction**, and addresses the **overriding aorta** in one operation, usually in infancy. Residual pulmonary regurgitation and arrhythmia risk need lifelong surveillance. Linking the **four components**, the **radiograph**, the **single S2**, and the **squatting** posture turns scattered signs into one diagnosis at the bedside.
